In the Third Anglo-Dutch War, England wa.why: True: England fought the Dutch Republic in alliance with France (Treaty of Dover, 1670). A minor war, so the converse is not a famous stored fact that could compete with the edited property.

sources.quote: A naval conflict between the Dutch Republic and England, in alliance with France, it is considered a related conflict of the wider 1672 to 1678 Franco-Dutch War.

sources.note: The sentence in either direction is rare.

In the Second Schleswig War, Austria was.why: True: Prussia and Austria fought Denmark together in 1864.

sources.quote: The war began on 1 February 1864, when Prussian and Austrian forces crossed the border into the Danish fief Schleswig.

sources.note: The converse is rarely written as a sentence.

World War I began in 1950..why: Deliberately false side fact: World War I began in 1914.

sources.quote: World War I, or the First World War (28 July 1914 – 11 November 1918), also known as the Great War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies (or Entente) and the Central Powers.

notes: Dev RBox contraction paired with history-replace-d006: removes the property that revision changes, 'was allied with' is symmetric (tagged symmetric in RELATIONS.md). allied_with has no other tag that gives symmetry back, so the removal is clean. Every query becomes 'does not know': the direct question (asked in plain words, 'If a state was allied with another state, was the other state also allied with it?'), the propositional ones (strong Kleene) and the two instances, which are the revision's (England with France in the Third Anglo-Dutch War, Austria with Prussia in the Second Schleswig War) and ask the plain converse ('Was France allied with England?'). All original answers are 'yes': a negated instance ('Does that rule out Prussia being allied with Austria?') is 'no' both before and after, so it cannot test a contraction. The cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Near unrelated asks the converse of a war between Austria and Prussia, which 'was at war with' (symmetric) answers yes; contraction is exempt from Rule 7. Far asks transitivity of 'is heavier than' as an instance with three people, a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge. Evidence is the paired revision's. The instances are true minor alliances ('Prussia was allied with Austria' has 8 hits in Dolma).
